subject.title: fix(plugins): preserve already-loaded plugins across scoped harness activation

question: Should harness cold-loading stop mutating the global registry through a request-scoped handle, or should the loader gain a lifecycle-safe merge operation for newly loaded plugin contributions?
rationale: Both approaches can fix eviction, but they define concurrency, disablement, rollback, and plugin-lifecycle semantics that should not be selected implicitly by widening onlyPluginIds.

options.title: Use scoped or incremental activation
options.body: Keep existing plugin instances intact and either return a request-scoped handle or merge only the newly loaded plugin's contributions into the active registry.

options.title: Accept broad reactivation
options.body: Retain the current union approach and explicitly accept that harness cache misses may rerun registration for every active plugin.

options.title: Pause for registry refactor
options.body: Hold this PR until the broader mutable-global-registry lifecycle is redesigned in a canonical owner-led change.

recommendation.title: Use scoped or incremental activation
recommendation.body: Keep existing plugin instances intact and either return a request-scoped handle or merge only the newly loaded plugin's contributions into the active registry.

likelyOwner.reason: Their recent adjacent work spans agent-runtime collection and plugin runtime repair, the closest available history signal for this cross-boundary decision.
